title: elmwood-credit-integration-call-notes-2026-09-16
content:
Call with Elmwood Credit - 2026-09-16
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood CS), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood RM), Michael Torres (Elmwood CTO), Sara Lin (Elmwood Product)

High-level summary:
- Elmwood wants Redwood for two main use-cases: (1) instant underwriting scoring explainability (few-shot explanations + structured output) and (2) customer support triage (short text classification + reranking).
- Priority is data isolation + PII handling; they will likely start on Private (VPC) but want a hosted POC to prove latency and cost numbers first.
- Key success metrics they care about: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for support triage, per-decision cost <= $0.002 equivalent tokens for underwriter pipeline, availability 99.9+.

Technical notes / integration constraints:
- Auth: Elmwood uses OAuth2 for internal services; they prefer short-lived tokens and want to integrate with their Okta instance. Action: check our Private/KMS docs for Okta SSO + token rotation examples.
- Data flow: underwriting will POST applicant JSON -> Redwood endpoint -> model returns structured JSON (score, rationale, risk_flags). They insist on deterministic output schema and an audit log for every request/response (retention 12 months).
- PII concerns: applicant SSN/PII will be sent in payloads. Elmwood requests (a) in-transit encryption (standard), (b) at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), and (c) ability to opt-out of storing prompt/response payloads in logs (no retention).
- Webhooks: Elmwood wants a webhook for async batched scoring results. They require HMAC-signed payloads and replay protection. Note: our webhook docs show HMAC + nonce; need to confirm replay window semantics.
- Model behavior: They want a conservative tone for explainability (avoid hallucinations). Suggested approach: use instruction-tuned model + structured output schema + strict parsing (json-schema validation). Discuss quantized model variants for Private deploy to reduce cost.

Gotchas / red flags:
- Tokenization mismatches: Elmwood's current token accounting uses GPT-like tokenizer assumptions for cost projections; we need to align on tokenizer used by the selected model to avoid billing surprises.
- Logging opt-out: Hosted API currently keeps request logs for 30 days for debugging; Elmwood requires complete opt-out. Need legal/ops sign-off on non-retention for enterprise private customers.
- Latency SLOs: Underwriting path has a tight SLO at 95p < 200ms - might be hard with larger-context explainability. Possibly offer two-tier approach: (a) lite-explain short rationale for fast path, (b) full explain async via webhook.
- Schema enforcement: Elmwood will reject any malformed JSON. Need to implement robust output parsing + fallback policy (e.g., if model fails to produce valid JSON, return error code + trigger retry via canary model).

Action items / next steps:
- [Avery] Send Elmwood Private deployment checklist + KMS/HSM integration guide by 2026-09-17. Linked doc: CONFLUENCE-ELMWOOD-INTEGRATION-001.
- [Jordan] Run a quick hosted POC with the recommended instruction-tuned model (small-medium size) and capture 1k sample underwriting prompts to measure tokenization and 95p latency. Target to have results by 2026-09-22. Create ticket: ELMWOOD-INT-42.
- [Priya] Draft data retention & logging exception language for legal review (specifically non-retention mode for enterprise) by 2026-09-20.
- [Michael (Elmwood)] Share sample payloads and example of current post-processing rules (they said Monday).
- [All] Sync on webhook HMAC/replay semantics - confirm acceptable replay window and nonce storage requirements.

Notes to self / quick follow-ups:
- Check Private deployment image sizes for quantized variants; estimate infra cost delta.
- Validate our JSON Schema enforcement library supports strict error codes Elmwood needs. If not, propose wrapper layer for validation + structured error responses.
- Prepare two demo scripts: (1) fast triage endpoint (low latency) and (2) explainability endpoint (async + webhook).

Open questions to clarify with Elmwood next call:
1) Exact retention SLA (they said 12 months for audit logs, but want prompt/response non-retention - need to reconcile).
2) Are underwriting decisions required to be signed/stamped for regulatory audit? If yes, we need an append-only log with signatures.
3) Volume expectations: they provided ballpark of 500k triage requests/month and 50k underwriting decisions/month - confirm daily burst patterns.

Slack refs / quick links:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C03ABC123/p1690000000
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ELMWOOD-INTEGRATION-001
- JIRA: ELMWOOD-INT-42

Status: Draft notes; will convert to a customer-facing one-pager after Jordan's POC results.

-- Avery
